clue.text: Patient fellow's account, list of duties, tasks etc

parts.note: Job, the biblical figure famed for his patience; the possessive just ties him to the account
an account of something is a description of it

explanation.surface: A long-suffering man tells his story, and the clue lists his chores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The patience of Job' is a proverb, so 'Patient fellow' is Job; 'account' is DESCRIPTION.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal statement of an employee's responsibilities is literally a list of the duties and tasks a post involves.

clue.text: Half bite very rotten veal and oyster?

indicators.note: only the first half of the word bite is used, its opening two letters
rotten veal has gone bad, so its letters are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone takes a nibble of bad veal and a shellfish and regrets it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rotten' rearranges VEAL to ALVE. The question mark marks the oyster as one example of the class.
explanation.definitionFit: An oyster is one example of a mollusc with a hinged two-part shell, the group the answer names.

clue.text: Little Ernest said to make money

indicators.note: said tells us the shortened name is spoken, and we enter a word with the same sound

parts.note: Ern is the short, familiar form of the name Ernest

explanation.surface: Young Ernest is told he must go out and bring in some cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little' shortens the name Ernest to ERN, which 'said' turns into a word sounding the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To gain income through work is to make money, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Messenger entertains tense attendant

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to take them in, so the messenger word holds the tense letter

parts.note: a courier carries messages and parcels
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A messenger keeps a nervous servant company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tense' looks like an adjective describing the attendant, but it is the grammar abbreviation T, which 'entertains' puts inside COURIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a royal court who waits on the monarch is an attendant at court.

clue.text: I get in fancy light

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or fanciful, so the letters are dressed up in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of getting into a stylish lamp or lighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light' looks like a noun, but here it is the verb, to set alight.
explanation.definitionFit: To set fire to something is to light it; both verbs mean making it start burning.

clue.text: Suit(e)?

parts.note: the optional e covers both a three-part suit of clothes and a three-part furniture suite

explanation.surface: A bare word with a bracketed letter, asking whether it means clothing or furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: With the e left out it is a jacket, trousers and waistcoat; with it, a sofa and two armchairs. The answer describes both.
explanation.definitionFit: A matched set of three garments or of three furniture items is described by this compound, so it fits either spelling.

clue.text: Indirect slanting

definitions.meaning: not straightforward, as with a roundabout remark
at an angle, neither vertical nor horizontal

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both roundabout in speech and sloping at an angle, two senses of one adjective.

clue.text: Hastily prepared without brief

parts.note: ex is Latin for out of or without, as in ex-dividend
something brief is temporary, lasting only a short time

explanation.surface: Something put together in a rush, without a briefing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' looks like a lawyer's or speaker's notes; it is the adjective meaning short-lived.
explanation.definitionFit: Made up on the spot, without preparation, the sense of an impromptu speech done in haste.

clue.text: Upset open vessel

parts.note: overt means done openly, not hidden
an urn is a vase-like vessel

explanation.surface: Someone knocks over a vessel that has no lid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'open' looks like a verb or a description of the vessel; it gives OVERT.
explanation.definitionFit: To upset a container is to knock it over, so the two verbs are synonyms here.

clue.text: Become less rigid about the French vote

parts.note: re means concerning or about, as in a letter heading
la is the feminine form of the in French
a cross on a ballot paper marks a vote

explanation.surface: Someone loosens up regarding how the French vote.
explanation.definitionFit: To unwind or loosen up is to become less stiff or tense, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Maybe reigning golf champion is a card

definitions.meaning: playfully, a monarch of golf clubs, the sticks a golfer swings
a playing card, the highest-ranking of the black suit with the trefoil symbol

explanation.surface: The current golf champion turns out to be quite a character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a card' also means an amusing eccentric person, which is what the surface wants.
explanation.definitionFit: The top court card of the trefoil suit is a playing card, and whimsically a sovereign over golf sticks.

clue.text: Unemployed Ian didn't like exertion initially

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the opening letter of each of the four words is taken

explanation.surface: Ian, out of work, never cared for effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without work is out of a job, an established sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Dignified sculpture with girl embracing queen

parts.note: a statue is a carved or cast sculpture

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so the girl's name wraps round the queen letter

parts.note: Sue is a girl's name
Q is the abbreviation for queen, as in chess notation

explanation.surface: A stately carving shows a girl hugging a queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Tall, graceful and dignified, like a statue in bearing, the sense used of an imposing person.

clue.text: Revolutionary device that will not work when it is dry

definitions.text: Revolutionary device that will not work when it is dry

parts.words: Revolutionary device that will not work when it is dry
parts.note: a turning wheel driven by a flowing stream, which stops when the stream runs dry

explanation.surface: A radical gadget that fails in a drought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suggests politics or innovation, but it only means turning round and round.
explanation.definitionFit: A mill wheel turned by a river or stream revolves and needs flowing liquid to work.

clue.text: Agree Ray confused in unclear situation

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Two people try to agree but are left bewildered by a murky matter.
explanation.definitionFit: An ill-defined situation that falls between clear categories is a common idiom for ambiguity.

clue.text: Young animal going round Corsica perhaps in collision

indicators.note: going round means encircling, so the young animal's letters surround the island word

parts.note: a pup is a young dog or seal
Corsica is a French island, and île is French for island

explanation.surface: A puppy runs round a Mediterranean island and crashes into something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' signals that Corsica is one example: an island, given in French because Corsica is French.
explanation.definitionFit: A crash involving several vehicles piling into one another is a collision.

clue.text: Poets from Nine Elms running riot

indicators.note: running riot means behaving wildly and out of control, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Poets from a London district go on a rampage.
explanation.walkthrough: Nine Elms is an area of south London by the Thames. The answer, usually football officials, is read whimsically as men who write lines of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Writers of verse produce lines, so whimsically they are men of lines, a crossword-only sense.

clue.text: Mythical female sailor went first

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
to lead is to go first, so led is the past tense

explanation.surface: A woman sailor took the lead in a legendary tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Something celebrated in legends and stories is legendary or mythical.

clue.text: Some contraband, an antiquarian handkerchief

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An antiques dealer is caught with a smuggled handkerchief.
explanation.definitionFit: A large brightly coloured kerchief worn on the head or neck is a kind of handkerchief.

clue.text: Round letter

definitions.meaning: shaped like a ring or disc
a printed notice or advertisement sent to many people at once

explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for ring-shaped and a noun for a mass-mailed leaflet.

clue.text: Owl flying over hill that's not very tall

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the second
a flying owl moves about, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a rise is a small hill or slope

explanation.surface: An owl flies above a low hill.
explanation.definitionFit: Describing a building of few storeys, so not reaching far upward, the opposite of a tower block.

clue.text: Start of sensuousness in marriage harmony

indicators.note: in places the first letter inside the marriage word

parts.note: a marriage is a union of two people

indicators.note: start of means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Sensual beginnings bring harmony to a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting or singing in agreement, together, is harmony; both suggest voices as one.

clue.text: Lengthy rambling

definitions.meaning: going on too long, as with a speech
wandering from point to point without focus

explanation.definitionFit: A wordy speaker is both tediously long and inclined to wander, two near senses of one adjective.

clue.text: Pitcher that, in pieces, is removed from the water

indicators.note: in pieces means the removed word is split, its letters taken out separately rather than as a block
is removed from says the letters of one word are taken out of the following words

explanation.surface: A jug that is broken into fragments is taken out of the water.
explanation.walkthrough: Strike out T, H, A and T one at a time from THE WATER and EWER is left. 'Pitcher' looks like a baseball player; it is a jug.
explanation.definitionFit: A large wide-mouthed jug for carrying water is a pitcher.

clue.text: Responsibility lying with you and me?

parts.note: on means resting upon or lying against
us is the pronoun for you and me together

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether the burden falls on the two of us.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints that the whole phrase reads as 'on us', which is where a burden lies.
explanation.definitionFit: A burden or duty that falls on someone is a responsibility, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Flame coming from short jacket

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the last letter of the jacket word is dropped

parts.note: a blazer is a light jacket, often in school or club colours

explanation.surface: Fire spreads from a cropped jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' looks like it describes the jacket; it takes the R off BLAZER.
explanation.definitionFit: A bright burning fire or flame is a blaze, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Stance I'm adapting relating to meanings of words

indicators.note: adapting means changing to suit, so the letters are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone says they are changing their position on what words mean.
explanation.definitionFit: Semantics is the study of meaning in language, so the adjective concerns the meanings of words.

clue.text: Lets off Anne and Leo struggling to come out well from a difficulty

definitions.text: come out well from a difficulty

indicators.note: struggling means floundering about, so the letters of the names and words are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Anne and Leo are struggling and someone releases them.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from a cat landing upright after a fall, so to emerge safely from trouble.
